groups.title: Testing Philosophy and Strategies
groups.question: You are writing tests for a Rails app with models, an API and Turbo-powered pages, and your fixtures keep breaking. Explain your testing approach.

followUps.RSpec model and request spec patterns: What do model specs and request specs each cover?
followUps.System tests with Capybara and browser d: What do system tests with Capybara catch?
followUps.FactoryBot for test data factories: Why use FactoryBot instead of fixtures?

evidence.text: Model specs test validations, associations and business logic.
Request specs test the full HTTP stack and responses.
Using both catches bugs in logic and in wiring.
Capybara drives a real browser through user flows.
It covers JavaScript and Turbo behaviour that other specs cannot.
They are slow, so they are kept to the most important flows.

notEnough: Only saying they test the UI.

evidence.text: Factories build records with sensible defaults.
Traits add variations, like an admin user.
Tests only set the fields they care about, which keeps setup clear.

notEnough: Only saying it creates test data.

groups.title: CI and Quality Gates
groups.question: Broken code keeps reaching main and test coverage is dropping. Explain how you would set up CI and coverage checks.

followUps.GitHub Actions CI pipeline for Rails: What does a GitHub Actions workflow for Rails need?
followUps.Code coverage with SimpleCov reporting: How does SimpleCov help, and what are the limits of coverage numbers?

evidence.text: It installs Ruby and the gems.
It starts a PostgreSQL service container and loads the schema.
It runs the full test suite on every pull request.
SimpleCov reports which lines the tests ran.
A minimum threshold can fail the build when coverage drops.
Covered lines are not necessarily well tested, so coverage is a guide, not proof.

groups.title: Containerization
groups.question: You want to run your Rails app in containers for production and local development with Postgres and Redis. Explain the setup.

followUps.Dockerfile for Rails production containe: What does the Rails-generated production Dockerfile do?
followUps.Docker Compose for local development sta: How does Docker Compose help local development?

evidence.text: It uses a multi-stage build with a slim Ruby image.
It precompiles assets during the build.
It starts the app with Puma, with migrations run as part of release.

notEnough: Only saying Rails has a Dockerfile.

evidence.text: Compose runs Rails, PostgreSQL and Redis together.
Services, ports and environment variables are defined in one file.
Every developer gets the same setup with one command.

groups.title: Cloud Deployment
groups.question: You are choosing how to deploy your Rails app: a platform like Render or your own servers. Explain both options.

followUps.Deploying Rails to Render or Railway: What does a platform like Render or Railway handle for you?
followUps.Kamal for zero-downtime Rails deployment: How does Kamal deploy with zero downtime?

evidence.text: They deploy straight from the GitHub repository.
They detect the Dockerfile or buildpack and provision PostgreSQL.
They run release commands like migrations before switching traffic.
Kamal builds a Docker image and pushes it to a registry.
It deploys the image to your own servers.
It starts the new version, checks its health, then switches traffic from the old one.
